title: ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you build a Demon Back like Yujiro Hanma from Grappler Baki
summary: NH explains that Yujiro Hanma's demon back is anatomically impossible to replicate exactly, but a thick, detailed back resembling it is achievable naturally by developing lats, traps and rhomboids. He lists deadlifts and pull-ups as the base, then dumbbell rows, pullovers, ring rows and shrugs, with set, rep and frequency options in the description.
claims: Yujiro's physique is unachievable for humans even with drugs, but using a fictional physique as inspiration is fine motivation fuel
The demon back is not literally possible because the muscles rearrange into a face, with exaggerated size and fiber separation
A lower-back 'smile' would require staying very lean, which makes building upper-back thickness harder, so ignore the lumbar aesthetics
The three key zones for a demon back are lats, traps and rhomboids; the lower back still gets enough work to grow and stay injury-resistant
Add back exercises to your existing split rather than following a short dedicated specialization burst
The upper back has the highest size potential of any body area, yet most people barely train it
Deadlifts and pull-ups are the bread and butter for upper back; deadlifts thicken the posterior chain, traps and rhomboids
Pull-ups grow the lats like nothing else with proper form; switching grips lets you do them more often, and accumulating volume on them is key
Deadlift once a week: 1x5, 3x3, or 1-3 sets of 2-5
Pull-ups: bodyweight 3 sets AMRAP daily or 5 sets AMRAP every two days; weighted 3x3 every 3 days
Prefer dumbbell rows over barbell rows for a better stretch from hip stability; torso angle shifts emphasis between traps and lats
Dumbbell rows twice a week for 4 sets of 6-12
Pullovers are the best lat exercise after pull-ups and help people who can't feel their back on pulls
Pullovers: 4 sets of 8-12 every 4 days, or 4 light sets of 4-8 every 2 days
Dumbbell rows and pullovers barely load the lower back, so you stay fresh for deadlifts
Ring rows are easy to recover from; do them bodyweight and elevate the feet for difficulty; pull with the back, minimize arm involvement
Bodyweight horizontal rows: 3 sets AMRAP every two days or 5 sets AMRAP every four days
Shrugs finish the demon back; change torso angle to target upper, middle or lower traps; use straps for back work except pull-ups
Shrugs: 4 sets of 10-15 every 3 days, or 4 light sets of 6-10 every two days
Start with just deadlifts and pull-ups and gradually add movements at a rate that fits your progression and recovery
exercises: any pull from the floor works; proper form
strict form; vary grips for frequency; bodyweight or weighted
torso angle to bias traps or lats
better stretch than barbell rows, spares the lower back
best lat exercise after pull-ups; improves back connection
bodyweight; elevate feet; pull with back not arms
